questions.q: For $y_1=e^x$, $y_2=e^{2x}$ (solutions of $y''-3y'+2y=0$), compute the Wronskian $W = y_1y_2' - y_1'y_2$.

questions.answer: $y_1'=-\sin x$, $y_2'=\cos x$. $W = \cos x\cos x - (-\sin x)\sin x = \cos^2x+\sin^2x = 1$.

questions.q: State the variation of parameters formula for a particular solution of $y'' + p(x)y' + q(x)y = g(x)$, given independent solutions $y_1,y_2$ of the homogeneous equation with Wronskian $W$.

sections.heading: A forcing term with no undetermined-coefficients trial form

questions.q: Solve $y'' + y = \tan x$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$ using variation of parameters.
questions.answer: Here $y_1=\cos x$, $y_2=\sin x$, $W=1$, $g=\tan x$. Since $\int\cos x\tan x\,dx=\int\sin x\,dx=-\cos x$ and $\int\sin x\tan x\,dx=\int\sec x\,dx-\int\cos x\,dx=\ln|\sec x+\tan x|-\sin x$, we get $y_p=-\cos x\left[\ln|\sec x+\tan x|-\sin x\right]+\sin x(-\cos x)=-\cos x\ln|\sec x+\tan x|$. General solution: $y = C_1\cos x + C_2\sin x - \cos x\ln|\sec x+\tan x|$.

sections.heading: A repeated root, with forcing dividing by x

questions.q: Solve $y'' - 2y' + y = \dfrac{e^x}{x}$ ($x>0$) using variation of parameters.
questions.answer: $r^2-2r+1=(r-1)^2=0$, so $y_1=e^x$, $y_2=xe^x$, and $W=e^{2x}$. With $g=e^x/x$: $\dfrac{y_2g}{W}=1$ so $\int = x$; $\dfrac{y_1g}{W}=\dfrac{1}{x}$ so $\int=\ln x$. Then $y_p = -e^x(x) + xe^x(\ln x) = xe^x(\ln x - 1)$. Absorbing the $-xe^x$ term into the arbitrary constant on $y_2$, the general solution is $y = C_1e^x + C_2xe^x + xe^x\ln x$.

questions.q: Solve $y'' - y = e^{2x}$ by variation of parameters, then check the particular solution using undetermined coefficients.
questions.answer: $y_1=e^x$, $y_2=e^{-x}$, $W=-2$. With $g=e^{2x}$: $\dfrac{y_2g}{W}=-\frac{1}{2}e^x$, integral $-\frac{1}{2}e^x$; $\dfrac{y_1g}{W}=-\frac{1}{2}e^{3x}$, integral $-\frac{1}{6}e^{3x}$. So $y_p=-e^x(-\frac{1}{2}e^x)+e^{-x}(-\frac{1}{6}e^{3x})=\frac{1}{2}e^{2x}-\frac{1}{6}e^{2x}=\frac{1}{3}e^{2x}$. Check by undetermined coefficients: try $Ae^{2x}$ (no resonance, since $2$ is not a root of $r^2-1=0$): $4A-A=1 \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{3}$. Matches. General solution: $y = C_1e^x+C_2e^{-x}+\frac{1}{3}e^{2x}$.
$y_1'=-e^{-x}(\cos2x+2\sin2x)$, $y_2'=e^{-x}(2\cos2x-\sin2x)$. Expanding $W=y_1y_2'-y_1'y_2$, the cross terms cancel and $W = e^{-2x}(2\cos^2 2x+2\sin^2 2x)=2e^{-2x}$.

sections.heading: Setting up variation of parameters (without full integration)

questions.q: For $y''+4y=\sec2x\tan2x$, with $y_1=\cos2x$, $y_2=\sin2x$, $W=2$, set up the two integrals in the variation-of-parameters formula (don't evaluate).

sections.heading: A polynomial forcing term, cross-checked against undetermined coefficients

questions.q: Solve $y''+y=x$ using variation of parameters ($y_1=\cos x$, $y_2=\sin x$, $W=1$), and verify it matches the undetermined-coefficients answer $y_p=x$.
questions.answer: $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$; $\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x+\cos x$. So $y_p=-\cos x(-x\cos x+\sin x)+\sin x(x\sin x+\cos x) = x\cos^2x+x\sin^2x = x$ — matching undetermined coefficients exactly (direct substitution: $0+x=x$ confirms $y_p=x$ is correct).

sections.heading: A repeated root with a forcing term dividing by x-squared

questions.answer: $r^2+2r+1=(r+1)^2=0 \Rightarrow y_1=e^{-x}$, $y_2=xe^{-x}$, $W=e^{-2x}$. With $g=e^{-x}/x^2$: $\dfrac{y_2g}{W}=\dfrac{1}{x}$, integral $\ln x$; $\dfrac{y_1g}{W}=\dfrac{1}{x^2}$, integral $-\dfrac{1}{x}$. So $y_p=-e^{-x}\ln x + xe^{-x}\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = -e^{-x}(\ln x+1)$. Absorbing the constant term, the general solution is $y=C_1e^{-x}+C_2xe^{-x}-e^{-x}\ln x$.

sections.heading: Summary: choosing undetermined coefficients vs. variation of parameters

questions.q: For $y''-y=e^{2x}\tan x$, explain why variation of parameters is required rather than undetermined coefficients.
questions.answer: $\tan x$ is not a polynomial, exponential, sine/cosine, or a product of these — the finite list of forcing types undetermined coefficients can guess a trial form for. Variation of parameters works for any continuous forcing $g(x)$, so it's required here.

sections.heading: A trigonometric forcing term via variation of parameters

questions.q: Solve $y''+y=\sec x$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$ using variation of parameters ($y_1=\cos x$, $y_2=\sin x$, $W=1$).
questions.answer: $\int\sin x\sec x\,dx=\int\tan x\,dx=-\ln|\cos x|$; $\int\cos x\sec x\,dx=\int1\,dx=x$. So $y_p=-\cos x(-\ln|\cos x|)+\sin x(x)=\cos x\ln|\cos x|+x\sin x$. General solution: $y=C_1\cos x+C_2\sin x+\cos x\ln|\cos x|+x\sin x$.

questions.q: For $y''-4y'+4y=\dfrac{e^{2x}}{x^3}$ ($x>0$), with $y_1=e^{2x}$, $y_2=xe^{2x}$, $W=e^{4x}$, set up the two integrals in the variation-of-parameters formula (don't evaluate).

sections.heading: A second forcing term with no elementary trial form

questions.answer: $\dfrac{y_2g}{W}=\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}$, integral $\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2)$; $\dfrac{y_1g}{W}=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$, integral $\arctan x$. So $y_p=-e^x\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2)+xe^x\arctan x$. General solution: $y=C_1e^x+C_2xe^x-\dfrac{1}{2}e^x\ln(1+x^2)+xe^x\arctan x$.
